text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A UK meta-regression of 236 elasticities found no overall practically significant adverse employment effect from minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The UK meta-regression found a possible genuine adverse employment effect in residential home care.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"An EPI review reports that most minimum wage studies find no job losses or only small disemployment effects.","cited_pids":["f3df8a818b8c#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A study of low-wage jobs found their number essentially unchanged over five years after minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["e0f83db9d354#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A study of the Great Recession found significant negative effects on employment and income for targeted low-skilled workers.","cited_pids":["ab2ba547baf0#1"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"The CBO projected that a $15 federal minimum wage would reduce employment by about 1.4 million people.","cited_pids":["6de9116294ca#3"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A review of the literature found no consensus on whether minimum wage increases cause disemployment for low-skilled workers.","cited_pids":["39a319a8bc00#0"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Disemployment effects from minimum wage increases are stronger for the least-skilled workers and teens.","cited_pids":[]}]}
